review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not continue the cumulative manuscript through another ordinary revision round. A new, sharply focused paper on whole-domain certification of implemented policies in convex capacity-constrained dynamic programs could merit evaluation, but R62 does not establish a method-specific Econometrica-level contribution for Neural Bellman Operators.
blocking_findings: The prospective evidence is adverse to the pure neural policy: all twenty pure-ReLU-minus-common expected-cost intervals are strictly positive.
The augmented policy obtains reliability from the common Bellman fallback; all augmented-versus-common cost intervals are unresolved and final bounds are effectively identical.
Pure ReLU and pure quadratic attain none of the twenty 1/32 targets, and the ReLU accuracy frontier is generally weaker than the quadratic frontier.
The common Bellman policy has the lowest recorded complete release work in all twenty attainable task-tolerance cells.
The multidimensional evidence remains tensor-grid dependent; the eight-dimensional cell certifies only the coarse 1/2 target.
The successful R62 theorem is a model-specific, method-neutral verifier rather than a general NBO training result.
Four fixed fitting seeds do not identify optimizer reliability, future-task performance, or restart work.
The baseline set omits strong adaptive conventional methods for convex dynamic programs even though the elementary common lattice already wins.
The normalized investment study supplies no calibrated or substantive economic result unlocked by NBO.
The 106-page article and 69-page active supplement, plus much larger complete companions, remain disproportionate to the focused certification result.
positive_findings: R62 certifies the actual acquired and rounded policy against the original continuous-action optimum.
Primitive convexity, Lipschitz, semiconcavity, interpolation, quadrature and action-cover accounts are explicit.
Pure fitted and common-augmented policies are retained as distinct economic objects.
The two-control case is a complete dynamic policy rather than a single action query.
Direct policy-cost differences are computed on fresh common paths rather than inferred from separate regret bounds.
Adverse policy-cost, accuracy, work and scaling evidence is preserved.
Source binding, clean-archive reconstruction and artifact provenance are unusually strong.

limitations: The reviewer did not rerun training, simulation, compilation, or timing; new executions would create new observations.
The reviewer spot-checked the central R62 theorem chain and audited all load-bearing records, but did not independently re-prove every inherited theorem.
The four fitting seeds are a fixed finite catalogue and support no population claim over future tasks or initializations.
Single-host timings plus a disclosed shared residual charge support no hardware-general performance inference.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
